0m6G8pDtzNs.title: The Job Nobody Wants in Japan
0m6G8pDtzNs.description: The Job Nobody Wants in Japan
0m6G8pDtzNs.transcript: It's impossible to get fired in Japan, but companies found something way worse. Imagine your boss walks you past your desk to a tiny room with no computer and no work. Just a ticking clock and a guy [music] with his feet up scrolling on his phone like he's on vacation. "Your new job," your boss says, "is nothing. Just sit here until 6:00." And you're thinking, "Wait, I'm getting paid for this?" At first, it's paradise. Then, your coworker starts staring when you walk past. The emails stop, and your old desk already has someone else's family photos on it. Every Friday, your boss pops his head in with a big smile to ask how you're enjoying your new role. Still, the guy in the corner has been doing [music] this for 3 years and looks happier than anyone in the building. So, if they want to pay you to do nothing, fine. You kick your feet up right next to him. Then, one Monday, you walk in and he's gone. His chair is pushed in, his desk is cleared, [music] and nobody will tell you where he went. You see, Japanese law makes it almost impossible to fire someone, but there's no law against making them miserable. So, they take away your work and your friends and just wait, because nobody can do nothing

7xS87iActkU.title: Why Perfect Railroads Don't Work
7xS87iActkU.transcript: He saw gaps into a railroad every 39 feet. You see, two companies are racing to build a railroad along a canyon so deep you can't see the bottom. And whoever finishes first gets the whole country's business. He's the youngest engineer on the job. And when his boss sees a finger-wide gap between every single rail, his face goes purple. You're wrecking my railroad. But he won't close a single one. The other company lays their rails end-to-end, perfectly smooth and finishes first. Their trains glide across the canyon without a sound, while his go clickety-clack over every gap. [music] The newspapers start calling it the clickety-clack line, and everyone switches to the quiet trains. Then summer comes, and something weird happens. His gaps start shrinking. In May, you can fit a coin in them. By July, barely a sheet of paper. And his boss is thrilled. See? Even your gaps know you were wrong. Meanwhile, on the perfect [music] railroad, the rails have started groaning in the afternoon sun, pushing against each other like they want to get out. On the hottest day anyone can remember, his gaps finally close, rail touching rail. [music] And halfway across the canyon, the perfect railroad kicks sideways like a snake right as a train rolls onto it.

aD73kaL_PtY.title: The Instinct That Makes You Crash
aD73kaL_PtY.description: The Instinct That Makes You Crash
aD73kaL_PtY.transcript: If you plant a tree beside an empty road, cars will steer right into it. You see, the road runs dead straight for miles, and the only thing [music] beside it is this one tree. But somehow somebody hits it every week. So the town nails a giant flashing arrow to it so nobody can miss it. Yet the crashes double. The tow truck guy starts parking out there with a lawn chair, and he's never made more money in his life. Eventually the sheriff drives out to see what's going on. He goes 15 miles an hour with both hands on the wheel and slams right into it. He climbs out furious, grabs an axe off the tow truck and chops the thing down while the tow truck guy watches his whole business fall over. The second his cruiser's fixed, the sheriff drives back out to enjoy his nice empty road and plow straight into the stump. So how does this keep happening? Well, it's called target fixation. After miles of nothing, that tree sticks out like a lighthouse, especially with a giant flashing arrow pointing at it, so every driver's eyes lock onto it and won't let go. And while they stare, their hands slowly turn the wheel toward it, [music] even when it's just a stump.

TRUkQ1wbV2E.title: How Mine Salting Worked
TRUkQ1wbV2E.transcript: He loaded the shotgun with gold and fired it into the walls of the mine. [music] His buddy just watches the gold vanish into the rock. So, we're shooting gold into a gold mine? You see, it's called salting. He's dug this mine for 10 years and found nothing but rock. And tomorrow, a rich guy is coming to buy it. So, he spent his last 100 bucks on gold dust instead. Next morning, the rich guy rolls up in a white suit and bangs his head on the first beam. But he's brought an expert, and the expert isn't stupid. He smashes a chunk of wall, swirls it in a pan, and gold flakes spin to the bottom. But under his magnifying glass, every flake is flat. Somebody shot this gold into the wall, but the rich guy just laughs. Why would anyone shoot gold into a wall? That's insane. And his buddy nods. Completely insane. So, the rich guy pays up. And while those two bolt with the money, he stays behind and pulls a stick of dynamite out of his suit. He's never mined a day in his life. So, he just lights it, tosses [music] it down the tunnel like a firecracker, and runs. And when the dust clears, there's a vein of real gold as thick as your arm, 10 ft past where the last guy gave up.

VS1Z_Q-Klt8.title: The Ancient Jar That Warned an Empire
VS1Z_Q-Klt8.description: The Ancient Jar That Warned an Empire
VS1Z_Q-Klt8.transcript: He put a bronze ball in a dragon's mouth and told the emperor if this ever falls out, run. The whole court burst out laughing. You see, there were eight dragons coiled around a giant bronze jar, each holding a ball over a frog's open mouth. But the emperor had the biggest army in the world and he wasn't about to run from a jar. Weeks later, a ball fell, but nothing happened. Not even a ripple in the emperor's mind. Now they laughed even harder. The emperor called it the world's most expensive toy and threw the inventor out of the city, jar and all. So, he dragged it up a hill outside the walls and lived there alone. Then, one night, a ball dropped. Then another. Then all eight at once. He ran to the city gates screaming for everyone to get out. "Hey, it's the toy guy. Did your frogs get hungry again?" The guards laughed him all the way back up the hill. The next morning, the palace was a pile of rubble. Inside the jar hung a heavy pendulum with a rod pointing at each [music] dragon. The slightest nudge and the pendulum swung into a rod, the rod snapped the dragon's jaw open, and the ball dropped. One ball meant a nudge from far [music] away. All eight meant the biggest earthquake the empire had ever seen was right underneath them.
